analysis.title: JPM US Market Intelligence Morning Briefing (November 2, 2026)
key_insights: JPM Market Intelligence stays Tactically Bullish and expects a Tech rebound. Its reasons are a Friday flush that tends to be followed by a rebound, a broadening trend, stabilization in Tech and positive November and post-midterm seasonality.

Positioning Intelligence finds that when the NDX is within about 6% of its all-time high and falls 3.5% or more, it tends to rebound about 3% the following week. The effect is stronger when the decline lands on a Friday, which suggests de-grossing rather than a change in fundamental views.

The Nov 2 Monetization Menu favors a barbell of Tech and Cyclicals with a heavier weight on Cyclicals. It expects the market to become more selective among AI winners and losers. Consumers and Financials can keep working if the yield curve steepens.
Europe could catch a bid and Value could return if the US and Iran move toward a deal. The bank cites Jan-Feb 2026 as the precedent for this kind of broadening.

The Oct 26 menu suggested hedges via long oil and Energy equities and long vol. The Oct 19 menu favored Tech exposure through pairs trades and derivatives, constructive Financials and Retailers, and Brazil and Japan internationally.

Midterm scenario analysis uses Bloomberg prediction-market odds as of Nov 1. Blue Wave (Dem House and Senate) is 66% with SPX -25bp to +50bp. Split Congress (Dem House, GOP Senate) is 26% with SPX +0.5% to +1%. Red Wave is 7% with SPX +1% to +1.25%. The other split (GOP House, Dem Senate) is 1% with SPX +25bp to +75bp.

In a Blue Wave, AI regulation would be hard to enact because Trump says he will not sign bills limiting AI expansion and Democrats cannot get a veto-proof majority. The risk is that the market uses the assumed liquidity increase to de-gross within the AI theme. Lower deficit spending could trim long-dated yields, and 'investigation risk' exists for business leaders tied to Trump donations, including MegaCap Tech.

A Red Wave could embolden Trump to continue in Iran until a US-friendly deal or Iranian capitulation. Continued elevated deficit spending could push long-dated yields higher. Democrats could pull Iran funding or force troop removal, but only after the new Congress is seated in January.
Early voting is up sharply, with 43mm votes cast, about 10mm more than in 2022. Polls from CNBC and Fox News now show corruption, not affordability, as the top voting issue.

Seasonality: the SPX has been up a year after every midterm since 1950, with an average gain of around 15%. Six-, nine- and twelve-month forward returns have a 100% hit rate since 1990. November is the strongest month on average this century.

The bank's answer to recession fears is no, based on record household net worth, strong cash balances, room to add debt capacity, record or near-record corporate margins, and AI not being a major hiring driver. It expects an AI capex decline to hit GDP growth metrics and possibly hyperscaler headcount more than the broader labor market or spending.
Consumer spending increasingly comes from investment accounts rather than checking or savings. A bear market would therefore bring a negative wealth effect, which is the main consumer risk.

The biggest non-AI risk is Middle East re-escalation. WSJ and AP satellite reporting shows heavy damage to US bases, and weapons inventories are reportedly depleted. That points to a limited-scope next wave of attacks and heightened diplomacy. Oil already prices a resumption, so upside to energy prices, bond yields and equity downside looks limited.

Oil markets price long-term disruption. The BBG 2027 Fair Value WTI swap is near $88 against $65-70 normal levels, and Brent trades about $20/bbl above fundamentals. This leaves fewer oil or Energy equity hedges to offset equity losses, so adding downside protection may be prudent.

Technicals (Jason Hunter): the S&P 500 is in a choppy range above key support at 7616-7643 and is threatening that zone again. Three of seven CTA trigger levels sit there. A break could extend toward the 7200s and then about 7000, and AI hardware ranges (SOX 10400-11000, KOSPI about 5000) are also at risk.

Hunter is watching whether the bearish pressure spreads from Tech to October's cyclical leaders (Financials, Consumer Discretionary, Materials). He will not suggest adding exposure until there are signs of bullish base building.

Last week the SPX fell 56bp and NDX fell 2%, while RTY rose 1.3%. NDX dropped 4.8% over the last two sessions on AI-trade fears. 9 of 11 SPX sectors rose, and the 2Y yield fell 9.4bp to 4.59% and the 10Y fell 6.6bp to 4.93%.

Pre-market Nov 2: futures are higher, led by NDX and RTY. WTI is down about 4% below $100 on Middle East diplomatic optimism. USD is lower for a fourth session and the curve is bull flattening. DRAM and SOXX are up 3.9% and 1.7%, and KOSPI is +2.2%.

Macro: Q3 real GDP grew 3.4% on the initial reading, with headline PCE 3.6% YoY and core PCE 3.1%, both above the prior month. Flash PMIs imply roughly 5% annualized growth with rising inflation impulses. This is a heavy data week with ISM, NFP and seven Fed speakers.
Feroli forecasts ISM-Mfg 54.5, ISM-Srvcs 55.5 (vs 54.9 prior) and NFP +75k with unemployment falling to 4.1%.

FactSet earnings update: with 60% of the SPX reported, blended revenue growth is 13.4%, EPS growth 30.2% and margins 14.9%. This is the second quarter where all 11 sectors show positive revenue and earnings growth. Mag7 blended EPS growth of 22.6% trails SPX493 at 32.6%, the first Mag7 shortfall since 22Q4.

Craig Cohen stats: GOOG fell 12.5% after earnings, its worst one-day move ever. The S&P 500 ex-AI stocks is at an all-time high. The share of S&P members above their 200-day average on track to rise 15+ points in a month while the index ends modestly lower, a breadth-versus-headline divergence. The equal-weight S&P is up nearly 5% in the month.

AAPL preview (Samik Chatterjee): FQ4 revenue forecast $112.9bn (+10% YoY), modestly above the guidance midpoint. He expects low to mid-single-digit growth guidance for 27Q1, with a $147.9bn revenue forecast (+3% YoY). iPhone revenue is $84.0bn (-2% YoY) on 69mm units (-18% YoY), with ASPs offsetting lower volumes.

Vol (Jade Bassil): spot/vol correlation in SPX and NDX has broken down in recent months, and NDX correlation is the least negative on record. Low net positioning, MMs holding a lot of vega, levered ETF growth (AUM +40% YTD), auto-call and exotic issuance, and spot at all-time highs all play a role.

Positioning Intelligence: October was bad for hedge funds. Global HF net returns fell about 4% on a rolling 20-day basis, and the global long-short spread was -2.2% MTD. Multi-Strats de-grossed heavily and Momentum exposure is at a 12-month-plus low, though quant de-grossing and elevated US Tech flows remain risks.

The US Tactical Positioning Monitor is at the 33rd percentile, retail sentiment is at the 6th percentile, ETF flows remain positive and CTA positioning is at the 44th percentile in US equities. The TMT vs Defensives sentiment gap at the 6th percentile echoes prior lows that were followed by Tech-led rebounds.

Sector and regional positioning: HFs flipped to buying Biotech and Med Tech, while Utilities rallied but HFs kept selling, leaving them least net-held. US Banks have strong November seasonality and HFs are net long Banks. EU positioning rebounded from the 5th to the 14th percentile, and China/HK positioning is the most bearish of any region at the 5th percentile.
The JPM D1 Split Congress Pair (JPMSC26P) has rallied to 2-year highs, with HFs more bullish on Split Congress longs, mainly through short covering in Health Care.

Key calendar: ISM-Mfg Nov 2, US midterms and JOLTS Nov 3, ISM-Srvcs and the Treasury refunding Nov 4, BoE decision Nov 5, NFP Nov 6, CPI Nov 10, Fed Dec 9, US government funding deadline Dec 11. The US-China trade truce has been extended through Jan 20, 2027.
Notable earnings: AAPL and PLTR after the close Nov 2, AMD, SMCI and ANET Nov 3, QCOM, UBER, DDOG and SNAP Nov 4, and ABNB, DKNG and NET Nov 5.

FactSet, with 60% of the SPX reported: blended (actual plus forecast) revenue growth is 13.4%, blended EPS growth is 30.2% and profit margins are 14.9%. The season is in line with expectations of 10%+ revenue growth and 25%+ EPS growth for a third consecutive quarter.
7 of 11 sectors show margin improvement, led by Energy and Tech. Margins compressed in Financials (-30bp QoQ), Discretionary (-30bp) and Staples (-10bp).
Mag7 blended EPS growth is 22.6% vs 32.6% for SPX493. Consensus for 26Q4 is 22.6% for Mag7 vs 30.8% for SPX493.
GOOG fell 12.5% after its earnings report, its worst one-day move ever and worse than GFC or COVID losses. A CNBC link notes AI is boosting Meta's ad business while hurting Google search.
Earnings this week include AAPL, PLTR, VRTX and ON on Nov 2 AMC, AMD, SMCI, ANET and PFE on Nov 3, UBER, DDOG, MCD and QCOM on Nov 4, and ABNB, COP, DKNG and NET on Nov 5.

risk_factors: Middle East re-escalation after the US midterms, the biggest non-AI risk.
AI trade concerns, including capital raising (CNBC), circular financing (WSJ) and legal issues (CNBC), plus a possible capex decline hitting GDP growth.
A break below SPX support at 7616-7643 could trigger systematic selling toward the 7200s and about 7000.
AI hardware groups (SOX 10400-11000, KOSPI about 5000) breaking multi-month range support could deepen sentiment deterioration.
Bearish pressure spreading from Tech to October's cyclical leaders such as Financials, Consumer Discretionary and Materials.
Blue Wave outcome could trigger de-grossing within the AI theme, and 'investigation risk' for MegaCap Tech and Trump-donor business leaders persists.
Potential quant de-grossing and still-elevated US Tech flows and futures positioning.
Persistent, elevated inflation (core PCE 3.1%) with rising inflationary impulses.
A negative wealth effect from a bear market would hit consumer spending, which is now more tied to investment accounts.
vol_and_positioning: Spot/vol correlation in SPX and NDX has broken down, with more spot up/vol up and spot down/vol down behavior. NDX correlation is the least negative on record. Skew has not realized because of more rotations than large correlated sell-offs.

Drivers cited by Jade Bassil: low net positioning, market makers 'still choking' on vega, levered ETFs (AUM +40% YTD), growing auto-call and exotic issuance on NDX and single names, and spot at all-time highs.

Global HF net returns were down about 4% on a rolling 20-day basis and about -2.6% MTD through Oct 29 (likely about -3.5% after Friday). The global long-short spread was -2.2% MTD, with Asia -1.5%, N. America -1.9% and EMEA -2.4%.
Prior -3z events in 20-day long-short spread saw positive forward 20-day spreads in 6 of 7 cases (avg +1%). Risks are potential quant de-grossing and elevated US Tech flows and futures positioning.

The US Tactical Positioning Monitor is at the 33rd percentile with a neutral 4-week change. HFs cut net leverage earlier in October and added slightly this week. Retail sentiment is at the 6th percentile, ETF flows are +1z and CTA US equity positioning is at the 44th percentile.
TMT-vs-Defensives sentiment spread and Social Media sentiment are both at the 6th percentile, echoing prior Tech-led rebounds (late Mar 2026, Mar/Apr 2025, Aug/Sep 2024, late Apr 2024, Dec 2022).

Utilities have the lowest net positioning of any major industry. EU positioning rebounded from the 5th to the 14th percentile, and China/HK positioning is the most bearish region at the 5th percentile.
Seven CTA trigger levels are tracked. Three (50-day MA, 100-day MA, 1-month momentum) sit in the 7616-7643 SPX support zone, and 3-month momentum joins by the middle of next week.
Hedging: a long vol and long oil/Energy equity hedge was suggested on Oct 26, but oil's already-elevated pricing leaves fewer offsetting hedges. Adding equity downside protection may be prudent.
geopolitical: US-Iran conflict: no consensus among equity investors on whether the US resumes kinetic activity, and oil already prices a resumption.
AP and WSJ satellite-imagery reporting shows Iran damaged 119 buildings across 13 US installations in the Middle East in the first two weeks of the war. This challenges earlier Pentagon statements.
Reports of depleted US weapons inventories (BBC, CNN, CSIS, Fox News, Military Times) call into question the intensity and duration of another wave of attacks.
US troops are in an engagement beyond 90 days without Congressional approval. Democrats could pull funding or force removal after the new Congress is seated in January.
Middle East diplomatic optimism and a ceasefire-play bid are weighing on crude pre-market, and OPEC+ left December oil output targets unchanged.
US approved a possible $2.1bn Patriot missile sale to Ukraine hours after Ukraine hit its first Russian refinery in 2 weeks.
The US and China agreed to extend the trade truce through January 20, 2027.
Upcoming political events include the US midterms on Nov 3, APEC leaders in Shenzhen on Nov 18-19, the US funding deadline on Dec 11 and the G20 in Miami on Dec 15-16.
China's October factory activity shrank, the third contraction in four months, while South Korea's exports nearly doubled on the AI investment boom.

tension_points.bull_case: A Friday flush of this size tends to be followed by a rebound (about 3% for NDX the following week), the broadening trend is strengthening, Tech is stabilizing and sentiment is at past-low levels that preceded Tech-led rebounds.
tension_points.bear_case: Weekend AI headlines on capital raises, circular financing and legal issues may give investors pause. AI hardware could break multi-month ranges (SOX 10400-11000, KOSPI about 5000) and a break of SPX support could trigger systematic selling.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An S&P 500 break below the 7616-7643 support zone, which could open a move to the 7200s and potentially 7000.

tension_points.bull_case: Even in a Blue Wave it is hard to implement AI-limiting policy because Trump will not sign such bills and Democrats lack a veto-proof majority. A dip would be a buying opportunity for AI bulls.
tension_points.bear_case: Many fear an AI sell-off on assumed higher regulation. The market could use the assumed liquidity increase to de-gross within the AI theme, and investigation risk for MegaCap Tech persists.

tension_points.bull_case: Oil already prices a resumption of hostilities and US capacity for another wave looks limited, so upside to energy prices, yields and equity downside is limited.
tension_points.bear_case: Re-escalation is the biggest non-AI risk, and with oil already pricing disruption there are few oil hedges to offset equity losses. Downside protection may be prudent.
